1

Project Overview

Project Operator

  • Sky Lounge Services
  • Winner of Qlayaat Airport Operation Bid (May 2026)
  • Based at Beirut Rafik Hariri International Airport
  • Holds Air Operator Certificate (AOC) and Ground Handling Certificate (GHC)
  • Specializes in private and commercial aviation
  • President: Ziad Monla (in partnership with Mez Company - Mohammad El Hout)

Geographic Location

  • Coordinates: 34°35' N, 35°59' E
  • Elevation: 75 meters above sea level
  • Area: 80 hectares
  • Phase 1 Capacity: 6–10 stands (Code C)
  • Phase 2 Capacity: 12–18 stands (Code C)
  • Ultimate Capacity: 25 stands (20 Code C + 5 Code D)
  • Initial Operational Capacity: 10–20 aircraft movements/day
  • Ultimate Capacity: 50–80 aircraft movements/day (after full development)
  • Throughput: Phase 1: 180 passengers/hour ,Phase 2 Ultimate Capacity: 400 passengers/hour

Project Objectives

  • Rehabilitate the airport for international flights
  • Develop infrastructure according to ICAO standards
  • Establish integrated air cargo zone
  • Provide modern air navigation services

Timeline

  • Rehabilitation & Equipment Installation: 12–18 months
  • Operational Testing & Certification: 3–6 months
  • Trial Operations: Q2 2027
  • Initial Aircraft Operations: Q2–Q3 2027
  • Official Operational Opening: Q3 2027
  • Phase 1 Development: 2027 – 2028
  • Phase 2 Expansion: 2028 – 2030
  • Phase 3 Comprehensive Development: 2030 – 2035
Important Note: The project aims to transform Qlayaat Airport into an ICAO-certified international airport, with a focus on developing the air cargo sector as a main economic driver for the region.
Runway Extension Note: Runway extension to 3,000m in Phase 2-3 is conditional and will only proceed if justified by traffic demand or wide-body cargo operations. All target aircraft (ATR 72, Dash 8, E175, B737-700, A320neo, B737 MAX 8) can operate from the existing 2,400m runway.

19A

Market Demand Analysis

Competitive Landscape

Beirut–Rafic Hariri International Airport

  • Primary international gateway for Lebanon
  • Capacity constraints during peak seasons
  • Located in southern Beirut, far from northern regions
  • Higher operational costs

Damascus International Airport

  • Major Syrian international airport
  • Limited capacity for regional cargo operations
  • Geographic advantage for northern Lebanon access
  • Cross-border logistics potential

Competitive Advantages of Qlayaat Airport

  • Proximity to North Lebanon: Direct access to Tripoli and surrounding industrial zones
  • Proximity to Syria: Strategic location for cross-border trade and logistics
  • Reduced Congestion: Lower traffic compared to Beirut, enabling faster turnaround times
  • Lower Operating Costs: Competitive landing fees and ground handling charges
  • Cargo Focus: Dedicated air cargo infrastructure and free zone potential
  • Industrial Integration: Close to planned industrial and logistics parks

Target Market Segments

SegmentDescriptionMarket Potential
Regional PassengerShort-haul flights to Middle East and MediterraneanHigh
Low-Cost CarriersSeasonal and year-round budget operationsMedium-High
Cargo & LogisticsExpress freight, perishables, e-commerceVery High
General AviationPrivate jets, business aviationMedium
Charter OperationsTourism, pilgrimage, seasonalMedium

Obstacle Limitation Surfaces (OLS)

ICAO Annex 14 Compliance: All obstacle limitation surfaces are designed in accordance with ICAO Annex 14 Volume I, Chapter 4, ensuring safe approach and departure paths for all aircraft categories.

OLS Summary (ICAO Annex 14)

Approach Surface

  • Inner edge: 280m, Distance: 60m from threshold
  • Divergence: 15%, Total length: 3,000m
  • Slope: 2% (Code 4)

Take-off Climb Surface

  • Inner edge: 180m, Distance: 60m from runway end
  • Divergence: 12.5%, Total length: 2,000m
  • Slope: 2% (Code 4)

Inner Horizontal Surface

  • Radius: 4,000m from reference point
  • Elevation: 45m above aerodrome
  • Circular shape

Transitional & Conical Surfaces

  • Transitional slope: 14.3% (1:7)
  • Conical slope: 5%, Total radius: 15,000m
  • All obstacles require assessment
Important Note: A comprehensive obstacle survey must be conducted during the detailed design phase to identify all existing and planned obstacles within the OLS. Any penetrations require coordination with DGCA and may necessitate obstacle lighting, marking, or removal.

Take-off & Landing Procedures

Departure Procedures

  • Standard Instrument Departure (SID) - QLAYAAT 1A
  • Runway 06: Climb straight ahead to 1,500 ft
  • Turn left heading 330° for VOR/DME
  • Transition altitude: 4,000 ft
  • Noise abatement: Reduced power climb

Arrival Procedures

  • Standard Terminal Arrival Route (STAR) - QLAYAAT 1B
  • ILS Approach Runway 24: Glide slope 3°
  • Circling approach: Minimum 1,500 ft MDA
  • Missed approach: Climb to 3,000 ft, direct VOR
  • Visual approach: Runway 06 preferred

Non-Aeronautical Revenue Sources

Diversified Revenue Strategy: The airport will generate substantial non-aeronautical revenue through ground handling, fuel farm operations, cargo warehousing, aircraft parking, free zone rentals, and commercial activities. Conclusions and Recommendations

Key Conclusions

1. Technical Feasibility

Qlayaat Airport project is technically feasible according to all applicable ICAO standards.

2. Economic Viability

Extended 25–30 year financial analysis demonstrates positive NPV ($15M–$45M) and IRR (8–12%). Project achieves payback within 12–18 years, consistent with global airport infrastructure benchmarks. Diversified revenue streams (cargo hub, free zone, ground handling, fuel farm) ensure long-term sustainability.

3. Development Impact

The project will contribute to creating 3-5 thousand direct and indirect job opportunities.

4. Regulatory Compliance

All designs comply with LARs and ICAO standards.

Recommendations

  • First Axis: Immediately begin licensing procedures and detailed designs
  • Second Axis: Establish project management authority with clear powers
  • Third Axis: Secure necessary funding for Phase 1
  • Fourth Axis: Develop partnerships with international cargo companies
  • Fifth Axis: Prepare training plan for local personnel
